purpose: Verify whether 0.28 mm is really the best layer height when print time, strength and light weight are all considered (user follow-up question).
method: Same process for all runs: P2S 0.4 nozzle, Generic PLA 12 mm3/s, 3 walls, 10% gyroid infill, >=0.8 mm top/bottom shells, tree-slim supports, identical geometry; ONLY layer_height and shell layer count changed (0.28->3 layers=0.84 mm; 0.20->4 layers=0.80 mm; 0.16->5 layers=0.80 mm).
time_effect: 0.28 mm is fastest: vs 0.20 mm it saves 3.74 h on the lower body and 9.28 h on the upper body (~13.1 h together with the panel); vs 0.16 mm it saves 6.74 h / 12.89 h.
weight_effect: With identical walls/infill the 0.28 mm bodies came out slightly LIGHTER (lower 373.95 vs 388.21 g at 0.20 and 389.14 g at 0.16; upper 802.97 vs 813.11 / 848.15 g). The panel is 1.74 g heavier at 0.28 (27.01 vs 25.27 g) because its shells round to 3x0.28=0.84 mm. Net all-part weight is 1203.9 g at 0.28 vs 1226.6 g at 0.20, so 0.28 does not cost weight.
strength_effect: 0.28 mm is NOT the strength-optimum: ~35% fewer layers (lower 786 vs 1100 at 0.20) means fewer interlayer bonds, and thicker layers generally reduce Z-direction (layer-adhesion) strength; in-plane stiffness is unchanged because walls/infill/shell thickness are unchanged. No physical strength test was performed, so no strength claim is made for either setting.
layer_height_limit: 0.28 mm is about 70% of the 0.4 mm nozzle diameter, the practical upper limit; not raised further (0.32 mm would be 80% and is not a reliable/checked setting, and no shipped P2S 0.4 process profile goes above 0.24).
verdict: 0.28 mm is the optimum on print time AND light weight (both measured); strength (layer adhesion) would favor 0.20 mm (strength/finish balance) or 0.16 mm (finest surface), at +13.1 h/+19.9 h total respectively and without weight benefit. Because the user asked for the fastest reliable setting while preserving structure/material, 0.28 mm remains the selected delivery; if strength is a hard requirement the 0.20 mm variant can be produced on request.
note: Numbers are slicer predictions from the same Bambu Studio 02.08.02.61 CLI; physical prints not tested.
